real_sample.derived_from: corpus/worlds/campack/level.dat (real, local-only, hash recorded in corpus/worlds/manifest.json; per corpus/worlds/README.md this real Fabric-modded server world was generated live by Cameron 2026-08-13)
real_sample.sanitization: Re-serialized from the real parsed NBT tree keeping only the Data-compound keys this reader inspects (GameType, Difficulty, DataVersion, Time, DayTime, LevelName, WorldGenSettings.seed) with LevelName replaced by a placeholder; every kept value and its original NBT tag type (int/byte/long/string) is byte-for-byte what the real level.dat contained. Drops WorldGenSettings.dimensions (a large mod-generator subtree carrying no player data but irrelevant to this reader) and every other Data key. Still a valid gzip-compressed big-endian NBT root Data compound -- same binary shape, far smaller.

notes: Real, current MSC 1 evidence (server 'campack', a Fabric-modded Java world, DataVersion 3465) where every legacy field WorldSlotManager.swift's extractors look for is present: Data.Difficulty is the legacy integer tag (2 == normal), Data.WorldGenSettings.seed is present directly (0), Data.GameType is 0 (survival), and Data.DayTime is present directly (10287, so extractDayTime's Java-preferred Data.DayTime path is used, never falling to Data.Time). Paired with java-real-modern-format-legacy-fields-absent, which is the SAME reader run against a real level.dat where none of these legacy fields exist -- together they show the extractors' fallback chains are not just theoretical, they are actually exercised by real servers Cameron runs today.
